title: Unity Anchor
concept: A way to name outside pressure together: when family, friends or strangers lean on you as a couple, it’s something coming at you both, not a flaw in either of you or in the relationship.
whenToUse: When disapproval or discrimination from outside (a relative, a friend, a stranger, a colleague) follows you home and starts turning into a fight between the two of you. If the pressure comes from your partner, this isn’t a Unity Anchor situation: use the Green Rule (Safety Gate), and the safety line below.
steps: Pause before reacting — don’t act on the comment or the look in the moment.
Trace the source — ask whether this is about the two of you or about them. Say it: “That’s coming from them, not from us.” Then ask what each of you needs: reassurance, a plan, or a chance to vent.
Name the unit — say it out loud: “We’re on the same side of this.”
Agree your response — decide together, as a team, how the two of you will respond next time — never how much contact your partner has with their own family, friends, money, phone or movements.

phrases.text: That’s coming from them, not from us.
We’re on the same side of this.
What do you actually need right now — reassurance, a plan, or just to vent?

working: The same dig comes at every family dinner, aimed at B. On the drive home A says, “That’s coming from them, not from us,” asks what B needs, and they agree how to answer it next time.
notWorking: Back home after the dinner, A asks B, “Well, did your mum have a point?” Now they’re arguing about her comment instead of facing it together.
activity: Name one recurring source of outside pressure on your relationship. Practise the phrase “We’re on the same side of this” out loud. Agree on one thing you’ll do differently the next time it comes up.
warn: Use it to decide together how you two respond to outside pressure, never how much access a relative gets to your partner. No tool is ever used to limit a partner’s contact with friends, family, money, phone or movement. Afraid of your partner, being threatened, or not free to say no? Stop: these tools are not for this. Get outside help.
